A secure and trustworthy 
blockchain-assisted edge 
computing architecture for 
industrial internet of things
Sasikumar Asaithambi1, Senthilkumar Nallusamy2, Jing Yang3, Sunil Prajapat4, 
Gyanendra Kumar5 & Pramod Singh Rathore6
The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) seeks to improve smart factory productivity by leveraging 
automation and scalability. For automation in industry, optimization, collaboration and protection, 
and scalability, the IoTs paradigm, technology for communication and information, and intelligent 
systems are integrated as a single organism. This article presents a blockchain-assisted safe data-
sharing mechanism that provides security requirements in the industry using IoT. End-to-end 
authentication is developed based on the blockchain’s reputation, and the smart contract is used to 
validate nodes’ security measures. Through integrity verification and categorization in node terminals 
and industry, the blockchain paradigm manages data collection and dissemination. An efficient proof 
of authentication (PoAh) consensus mechanism is created using the blockchain network to build a 
collaborative network to preserve logs and verification data in the industrial IoT. It accomplishes 
trustworthy authentication and endpoint activity tracing, and edge computing is used in blockchain 
nodes to offer device authentication processes that utilize smart contracts and PoAh. According to 
an experimental study, the proposed architecture lowers the authentication time and obtains a high 
response rate. The proposed system’s service time shows the efficiency of PoAh-based blockchain 
architecture for industrial IoT compared with existing works. Finally, we evaluated various block sizes 
to ensure an efficient transaction rate. The outcomes demonstrate the practicality of the suggested 
and put-into-practice architecture, distinguished by enhanced data audibility, device data ownership, 
security, and privacy while utilizing decentralized storage.
Keywords Authentication, Blockchain, Edge computing, Industrial internet of things, PoAh

replies.

computing machines, and IoT can all work together in the cloud. With the help of many automated systems 
and communication methods, such a diversified platform can improve customer service. The IoT has enormous 
potential to enhance the features and capabilities of any service it provides or supports, regardless of the use case. 
An additional dimension of difficulties will arise because of current use cases and near future ones. Centralized 
data storage is a big obstacle. The existing storage mechanism in IoT system implementations, the quantity of 
data gathered in one place, and the number of IoT devices all go hand in hand. Concerns about data ownership 
and administration will arise because of this central data consolidation. Attackers may find centralized data 
aggregation appealing and manipulate the IoT system to their advantage, leading to catastrophic consequences3.
Within the IoT environment, this raises confidentiality and security issues. A system that can use the 
current edge computing platform’s features and address some of these problems is needed to facilitate the scaled 
interconnected future. IoT systems must interact and integrate with their surroundings safely and effectively 4. 
These IoTs technologies provide enormous amounts of data that can be instantly processed and analyzed to aid 
decision-making process. Such processing should occur near the network’s edge to maximize timeliness and 
minimize bandwidth needs. Edge computing can interpret data and make choices at the network’s edge. As a 
result, it is necessary to investigate the advantages and disadvantages of edge computing in IoT.
Edge computing: an overview
The massive influx of data from the IoT is straining cloud computing due to expensive bandwidth and high 
latency. However, to meet the fundamental needs of the industry in areas such as real-time enterprise, artificial 
intelligence, security, and privacy, edge computing offers a service computing model that is near objects or data 
sources, enabling rapid response to various services 5. In this section, we will outline the key features of edge 
computing. With edge computing, processing power is physically and conceptually near to the endpoints. This 
means that everything from data production to data processing to data utilization occurs near the data source, 
ensuring a near-instantaneous response to requests from terminals.
Edge servers can self-recover and operate independently in a network outage. The central cloud is responsible 
for executing flexible computational offloading and assigning tasks to appropriate edge servers. Many diverse 
and adaptable edge devices are available to meet the increasing demands of the IoTs. In addition, servers located 
in edge computing surroundings may enhance cloud computing capabilities by providing these nearby diverse 
edge devices with enhanced storage, processing, and communication features. These enhanced features include 
increased data storage capacity, faster data processing speeds, and improved communication bandwidth, all 
of which contribute to the efficiency and performance of edge computing. This shifts resources away from the 
cloud facilities and onto the edge, reducing the load on the cloud layer. Restricted Data Access is unnecessary to 
transport data to distant clouds since edge devices can collect and analyze data locally. Thus, security is improved 
to some level since most information, particularly private data, does not have to pass over the network.
With increasing processing power and storage space, the architecture progresses from the device layer to 
the core layer and back again. The device layer comprises many diverse IoT devices with limited resources 
and computing capability6. These devices include sensors, RFID tags, recording devices, automobiles, outside 
units, etc. Their primary purpose is to gather, send out, and upload raw data, serving as the data collection and 
transmission hub of the IoT system. The edge layer supplies processing, storage, and network bandwidth to 
devices at the network’s periphery, acting as servers from a computational standpoint. The computer offloading 
methodologies of jobs and the coordination of associated resources are crucial to the edge layer because of the 
nature of edge server capacities and network architecture. The core infrastructure typically indicates the cloud 
layer, whose topologies are comparable to cloud computing. The cloud layer must be invoked to finish the jobs 
the edge layer cannot handle. In addition, the cloud layer can adapt the edge layer’s deployment techniques in 
real time according to the constantly changing allocation of edge resources.
Blockchain: an overview
Everyone has been talking about blockchain technology ever since Bitcoin was developed. A blockchain is a 
distributed ledger technology that can record financial transactions 7. A hash label connects the blockchain’s 
most recent block to the one that came before it. In particular, the following data can be stored in a blockchain 
block:
 1. Information on the activities, including the time, date, and amount.
 2. Facts regarding the participants in those transactions.
 3. A distinct hash code that distinguishes one block from another.
A new block is appended to the end of the blockchain for each transaction. Since the blockchain stores all 
transactions in a public ledger, which is a type of blockchain that is open to everyone, it is entirely transparent. 
Users’ identities and other sensitive information will be maintained securely on the public blockchain to protect 
their privacy8. In addition to the hash of the data inside it, each block on the blockchain also includes the hash 
of the block that came before it. Therefore, a decentralized distributed ledger technology (DLT) is a common 
way to describe blockchain. It is challenging, if possible, for a hacker to alter a blockchain transaction without 
changing the hash of every block that follows it. Blockchain is well-suited for use in several industries because 
of its inherent security, which includes finance, healthcare, government agencies, managing supply chains, and 
many more9.
Blockchain transactions are confirmed and verified by a “consensus protocol, ” as opposed to conventional 
systems that rely on a central authority to do the same. Using a consensus method, every node in the blockchain 
network may agree on the blockchain’s present state10. A consensus algorithm must be implemented to ensure 
that all blockchain nodes agree on the present condition of the chain every time a new block is produced (via

transactions). The consensus process is also performed when a new node is added to the blockchain. Therefore, 
consensus algorithms play a crucial role in establishing the trustworthiness of every node in the blockchain, 
ensuring the blockchain’s dependability and security. Proof of Capacity, Proof of Stake, Proof of Burn, and 
Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance are among today’s most widely utilized consensus algorithms. Smart 
contracts are implemented on a blockchain to guarantee that the transactions adhere to the specified conditions 
and limitations.
Smart contracts, implemented with just a few lines of code, ensure that each transaction adheres to pre-
agreed conditions. This efficient automation relieves you from the manual task of confirming transactions, 
empowering you to make rapid and accurate decisions. The decentralization, immutability, and transparency of 
blockchain further enhance its appeal.
 (1) Decentralization: Before blockchain technology became popular, there used to be a single location where 
all the data was kept, and everyone could access it through this one location. One point of failure, attack 
susceptibility, and other problems characterize centralized systems. Because all the nodes in a decentralized 
system have the data, it is possible to circumvent these problems with centralized systems.
 (2) Immutability: Data recorded on a blockchain cannot be altered because of consensus algorithms. Block -
chain is perfect for use in many industries because to this quality, including banking, supply chain manage-
ment, regulation etc11.
 (3) Transparency: Each blockchain technology is perpetually open source. Anybody sees every transaction on 
the blockchain. Since changes to the blockchain network require approval from most nodes, the technology 
or transactions remain safe despite their transparency. Complex cryptography techniques are used to con-
ceal user information12.
Implementing blockchain technology in decentralized systems, such as IoT, presents several significant 
challenges despite its numerous advantages. Running consensus procedures, like PoW , on the blockchain causes 
considerable network latency and substantial energy consumption, a severe issue. For dispersed IoT networks 
where IoT devices have limited resources, this can be a dealbreaker for blockchain applications. The low data 
transfer rates of blockchain platforms is another issue.

network, IoT becomes an essential subject. The security challenges of edge computing-based IoT systems are 
shown in Fig. 1.
• Precision It indicates how near a node’s computed trust value is to its fundamental or trust value when all

• Security If you want to be sure your edge-based IoT system is secure, you need to build trust. When it comes

• Accessibility It means that the trust management system can guarantee that all network services will be fully

• Dependability Trust management approaches rely on it as a crucial parameter. The lifespan of the edge-based 
network guarantees that all functionalities perform correctly.
• Diversity Typical components of edge-based IoT include diverse subnets, nodes, edge nodes, and edge servers. 
For a trust management system to meet the diversity criteria, it must be able to accommodate objects with 
varying degrees of complexity, computational capacity, and use of energy.
• Lightweight Restricted devices and networks are a part of IoT systems that operate at the edge. Because of this, 
edge-based IoT trust management frameworks need to be small and efficient enough to function effectively 
across a wide range of IoT nodes, networks, and servers, even when faced with limited resources14.
• Scalability and flexibility The IoT systems are constantly evolving, edge-based IoT must be very flexible and 
peers participating in trust-based transactions can change quickly. Additionally, regulations for assessing the 
credibility of edge servers and nodes are subject to frequent device changes, and the availability of their re -
sources might vary widely 15. A new node can be introduced to the system, and a different application may 
need connectivity to these edge servers and nodes; nevertheless, an IoT device’s transmission and storage 
costs do not scale with the number of devices in the network.
Motivations and contributions
Blockchain and IIoT systems are inherently different, posing a significant challenge in their integration with 
edge computing. The limited resources of IoT devices and the need for a scalable security solution in the face of 
extensive IIoT networks further complicate industry system. However, this study proposes a private blockchain-
based architecture for the IIoT network that is lightweight, scalable, and specifically designed to tackle these 
difficulties. The potential of this proposed design is immense, offering a ray of hope in addressing the challenges 
of IIoT integration with blockchain. The following are some of the most important contributions of the proposed 
system.
 1. Integrating blockchain with IoTs in a way that works for smart factories is a significant opportunity. This 
study proposes a private, decentralized, blockchain-based IIoT network that is not only lightweight but also 
highly extensible, ensuring its adaptability to the evolving needs of the industry.
 2. In the proposed architecture, first step is implementing small nodes that use virtual machines to conduct 
asymmetric cryptography in real time. Secondly, the primary blockchain network implements a (PoAh) sys-
tem. This system, which is both scalable and compatible with the IoT, ensures that only authenticated devices 
can participate in the blockchain network, thereby enhancing its security and reliability.
 3. Further, we examine the blockchain integrated IIoT paradigm’s security needs. We specifically examine the 
way blockchain might help with important industry security services such as trust management, secure data 
sharing, device registration, and device authentication.
The outline of the rest of the article is as follows: Sect. 2 covers the current state of blockchain technology as it 
pertains to IIoT systems. Section 3 details the edge computing-enabled blockchain architecture. Section 4 details 
the proposed architecture and its operation model. Section 5 provides a comprehensive analysis of the system’s 
efficiency. Lastly, Sect. 6 provides a concise summary16.
Related work
The (IIoT) has emerged as a game-changing technology in the past decade, drawing heavy interest from 
academics looking to improve manufacturing operations 17. Several industries have seen the benefits of the 
IIoT in areas such as environmentally friendly procedures, proactive upkeep, precise real-time data processing, 
and more. When used in industrial settings, blockchain technology may ensure human rights are respected 
while providing traceability and openness. In this section, we summarize several recent studies that have 
addressed blockchain’s potential uses in IIoT. Minoli, D., and Occhiogrosso18 state that IoT devices may benefit 
from blockchain for legitimate transactions and untampered archives in their research using blockchain as an 
IoT platform. According to them, the most challenging part of implementing blockchain technology in IoT 
devices is finding a suitable hosting infrastructure. Testing both fog and the cloud as potential implementation 
platforms, they find that fog is superior. In their work on edge computing for blockchain in endpoints with 
restricted resources, Feng et al.19 introduced a prototype. They proved that mobile devices may access and use 
edge network computing power to enable blockchain in their apps. As more miners sign up for the network, the 
integration also benefits service providers, according to their testbed and experimental findings.
To help video streaming systems employ blockchain for transcoding, Liu et al.20 suggested a methodology for 
distributing resources in edge computing. They devised a system to incentivize transcoding and looked at two 
ways to remove the workload from edge computing. Their simulation findings confirmed the model’s ability to 
maximize average profits in offloading and dynamic allocation of resource schemes. To determine if it would be 
possible to use blockchain technology and peer-to-peer (P2P) communication to create a decentralized private 
design for IoT applications, Alzoubi et al. conducted a systematic literature study on the topic21. Their research 
revealed that three problems anonymity, adaptability, and integrity impeded smooth integration. Their research 
showed that identities are the exclusive means of guaranteeing anonymity, that integrity depends on PoW’s 
difficulty and the substantial number of honest miners, and that flexibility is, by coincidence, constrained by 
PoW’s complexity.
Security and accountability of recorded resource administration status data are critical components of an 
effective resource management system. Integrating blockchain technology into such architecture may guarantee 
data security and provide a reliable environment. To achieve the methodically integrated management of 
resources and the decentralized construction of ecosystems during the creation and activities (DevOps) process,

To fortify data against attacks such as identity-revealing, session hijacking, relay, and man-in-the-middle, a

Zhang et al.29 presented the application of industrial IoT for effective certificate-less signing in cloud-assisted

Gai et al. 37 built IIoT based on a blockchain that uses asymmetrical privacy. This piece aims to bridge the

The rising significance of safe and effective data processing systems to handle the massive amounts of data 
produced by industrial applications is highlighted in the above literature. Because edge computing can process 
data closer to the source, reducing latency and bandwidth usage has become an essential component. Traditional 
edge and cloud-based approaches frequently need more security and confidence than blockchain’s decentralized, 
immutable ledger provides. Related work has investigated several frameworks that combine edge computing and 
blockchain to manage identities, encrypt data, and preserve integrity among dispersed devices in IIoT networks. 
However, the adoption of many existing models in IIoT systems with limited resources could be improved by 
scalability, energy consumption, and interoperability issues. Limitations still exist despite these developments,

Lightweight blockchain for resource-limited edge devices
Blockchain demands a lot of processing power for consensus techniques and sufficient space to store the whole 
blockchain when it allocates resources in edge computing. Therefore, the most critical problem in blockchain-
based resource allocation is enabling blockchain expansion in edge computing. In 39, researchers have looked 
at several ways to improve lightweight blockchains. An efficient LiTiChain blockchain is suggested in 40 to 
accommodate the edge-enabled IoT system. LiTiChain uses an End-time Ordering Graph (EOG), a tree-like 
data structure in blockchain technology, to keep track of time-sensitive activities and blocks. To save storage 
space on the edge nodes, the EOG depends on the sequence of the end time and deletes expired blocks. The 
design of EOG is adjusted to preserve the order of blocks using algorithms for k-height inclusion and deletion/
renewal of a block.
Our proposed blockchain, tailored for edge computing, is not just a theoretical concept. It is a practical 
solution that ensures fair storage and speedy, effective use of blocks. The article presents solutions for catching 
recent blocks and the best distribution of storage space for blocks41. In addition, nodes are incentivized to own 
more tokens and retain more data using an enhanced PoS consensus process tailored for edge devices with 
limited battery life. To overcome the mathematical mystery of PoW consensus, a successful consensus technique 
is suggested in42 that uses the expectation-maximization algorithm with polynomial matrix factorization as its 
basis.
Edge computing-enabled blockchain
Edge devices may support blockchain with minimal resources thanks to edge computing, a new paradigm. Put 
differently, edge computing is a facilitator of blockchain resources. A MEC-enabled blockchain architecture 
for IoT is presented in 43, wherein cloud computing resources may be purchased by IoT devices using mining 
as a service. In 44 MEC servers are separated into authentication servers (AS) and computing servers (CS) to 
reduce computing and transmission costs for vehicles with limited resources. Batch confirmation and anonymity 
techniques improve privacy and authentication effectiveness. The plan mostly depends on MEC servers’ 
dependability and accessibility, which might be problematic in areas with inadequate infrastructure or erratic 
connectivity.
Feng et al. 45 introduces PBAG, a blockchain-based authentication mechanism for the Internet of Vehicles 
(IoVs) that protects privacy. IoVs allow for real-time communication between infrastructure and automobiles, 
but they also present privacy concerns like monitoring and security risks like message forging. It uses a dynamic 
updating method supported by blockchain technology to guarantee certificate validity instead of relying on 
laborious Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs). Due to its heavy reliance on trusted authority and blockchain 
infrastructure, the protocol may be difficult to implement in rural or impoverished areas. It offers defense against 
common assaults and has been tested through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in high-demand IoV 
scenarios. It can be challenging to balance traceability and privacy, and if the traceability mechanism is broken, 
unexpected dangers could occur. In46, two mining strategies are examined to maximize earnings for edge service 
suppliers and miners: immediate reporting following practical computing and selective reporting following 
successful computing. To increase the adaptability of blockchain, an architecture for edge computing-based 
parallel computation has been developed 47. The blockchain, acting as a decentralized database, plays a crucial 
role in synchronizing and preserving the activity information of IoT gadgets, thereby ensuring data integrity and 
security. Edge nodes are set up to carry out the parallel analyzing method by providing the verification service.
The research has provided valuable insights into the practicality of combining blockchain technology with 
edge computing for IoT applications. This knowledge, derived from studies that have used integration as a 
launchpad for applications, delves into the broad architectural challenges of integration and the intricate world 
of mitigating specific blockchain concerns. Our research has focused on developing a practical platform for 
implementing blockchain services in the IoT, with specific emphasis on meeting the recognized critical security 
and flexibility requirements for safe, decentralized storage.
The proposed blockchain enabled edge computing architecture for IIoT
The proposed structure aims to make safe handling of operations possible in intelligent industrial settings. 
These functions include initializing the system, storing data from sensors and actuators, and providing reliable 
industrial operations to clients. The following subsections give a brief description of each of these operations.
System architecture
We present a high-speed blockchain-enabled edge computing architecture tailored for medical applications. The 
proposed architecture, as depicted in Fig. 2, offers significant benefits. IoT users can efficiently dispatch tasks to 
the industry through a unified interface. The blockchain structures, which specify data dependencies, streamline 
the organization of industry tasks. The manager, leveraging the blockchain structure of operations, resource 
utilization, and network circumstances of edge servers, devises a coordination strategy.
Simultaneously, the manager leverages the blockchain to ensure the security and authenticity of user 
identification. If a user’s actions are deemed unauthorized, the manager can immediately halt the allocation of

computer resources. The edge servers, in turn, execute the tasks, download and install the necessary container 
images, and report the outcomes to the management. Each user is affiliated with an authorized network, which 
responds to computed models. The job computation results, and user-identifying data are securely stored on the 
blockchain, ensuring the highest level of security and protection.
All approved user identification data is managed by the gateway and uploaded to the blockchain, which 
is continuously updated. The blockchain’s data is readily accessible upon receiving a query response from the 
management. In this setup, users can enjoy the benefits of minimal latency, straightforward implementation, 
and control over an edge computing service. The blockchain, with its robust security and reputation protection, 
ensures the service’s integrity. User clients and associated IoT devices seamlessly register in the blockchain 
system during the setup phase. This process is crucial for enabling user and device re-authentication. User and 
device registration are the final stages of the registration process, which is designed to be user-friendly and 
straightforward.
Main components
1) The manager is responsible for collecting data, task separation, subtask coordination, interim outcome 
conservation, user authentication, and resource handling. In contrast to conventional decentralized edge 
computing designs, the proposed architecture securely encrypts the system using blockchain technology and 
controls the entire system worldwide.
2) The processes are distributed across edge servers. They listen to the work demands and provide the 
management with resource data. Upon receiving user tasks, it will obtain and launch the necessary container 
pictures and establish ports for interaction. The manager will arrange for edge servers to process the job and 
provide the results after receiving the raw data. Since the edge servers are arranged as a changing system, they 
may be quickly added to and deleted from the platform. As a result, edge computing platforms’ expansion and 
reliability are assured.
3) Industry: Every user has an associated IIoT. In response to the relevant user, the industry will act according 
to the directions given by the manager. The edge servers’ calculations are used to determine the instructions. 
Specific data are synced to the blockchain for investigation or additional authentication.
4) First, a system administrator creates a new, distinct ID for each client. The admin then submits this ID as 
an activity request to the blockchain nodes. Using a smart contract, the blockchain node verifies the ID’s presence 
in the system. If the ID is not in use, the transaction is permitted. A new block is created and disseminated to 
all the blockchain nodes. The blockchain uses its private key, a crucial security measure, to generate a user ID 
certificate. This certificate is given to the administrator if the user has properly registered. Administrators can use 
their private keys to access certificate data.
5) Sensors and actuators are found in the suggested design’s physical layer. The data from the sensor or 
actuator is preprocessed as needed, and then the virtual machine, acting as a data handler, forwards it to a tiny 
node in the blockchain application layer. The portable node processes the device registration demand and sends 
an extra transaction request to the blockchain node. In the blockchain network, an intelligent contract confirms 
the device ID. A fresh block is created and dispersed across all nodes on the blockchain after the PoAh procedure 
is finished.

Blockchain integration
The blockchain serves as the decentralized verifier, ensuring the security and reliability of the system. It stores 
and validates transactions produced by decentralized entities. The hash values of user-submitted data and the 
outcomes calculated by edge nodes form a transaction’s information structure. Each transaction contains digital 
signatures and IDs of the relevant edge servers and medical devices, along with a timestamp. The four smart 
contracts document and validate the data analysis procedure, further enhancing the system’s security. The 
Identity contract plays a crucial role in the system, overseeing all entities, including edge servers and dispersed 
IIoT users. Its oversight provides a sense of control and management, ensuring the system’s smooth operation.
Submission contract This contract serves as an interface, enabling edge servers and users to securely contribute

Consensus model: proof of authentication
This study proposes a novel consensus mechanism, called Proof-of-Authentication, to create a distributed ledger 
that is durable and compact for endpoints with limited resources. During block confirmation, this consensus 
technique adds a verification method48.
The network precipitants create transactions (Trx) at the start of the process by assembling sensed or 
collected data into blocks. Blocks are shown in the illustration as B = {Trx1, Trx2, …, Trxn}. The nodes broadcast 
the blocks so that other reliable nodes in the network may review and validate them. We adhere to the typical 
IoT deployment procedures to establish the initial trustworthy node-set based on geographic location. Y ou can 
connect to trusted nodes from anywhere in the network. The ElGamal cryptosystem is used by the suggested 
model for encryption and decryption., i.e.
 y = gx (mod p)
Where y denotes the public key PuK, and x denotes the private key PrK. Every network device knows the big 
prime numbers for generator function g and modulus operation p. The network user signs the block using its 
private key PrK, or x and makes the public key PuK, or y, available to the network before the block transactions.
The suggested protocol is specially made for dispersed networks with limited resources, like the Internet of 
Things, where a small number of trustworthy nodes with a minimal trust value will be initialized during network 
deployment, and other network devices will have a zero-trust value or “tr = 0. ” The trust value of an authenticated 
node is increased by one upon successful block authentication. Likewise, every forged block authentication will 
cause the trust value to drop by ‘tr = 1’ . Other untrusted nodes in the network can also recognize the authenticated 
block to obtain trust value, or “tr = 0.5, ” after node authentication by the trustworthy node. Crucially, detecting 
fraudulent block authentication might result in a high trust score, or “tr = 1” . When a trusted node’ s trust 
value falls below the threshold “tr < th, ” it may be eliminated from the process through this trusted assessment 
procedure, and a regular node can continue to the authentication process. Here, trustworthy nodes are given an 
initial trust value of “tr = 10” and a threshold of “th = 5. ” The authentication process is depicted in Fig. 3.
When the trustworthy node receives the block for validation, it looks for the source public key, or y, to verify 
the signature. The public key is utilized in this work’ s asymmetric cryptography to validate signatures. When 
everything else is publicly accessible, an attacker cannot obtain the private key or x. The discrete log problem is 
this one. Following successfully verifying the signature, the trustworthy node assesses the Media Access Control 
(MAC) address and does a second assessment by comparing it with the received one. The trustworthy nodes 
with PoAh identity broadcast confirmed blocks following successful authentication. Then, individual network 
users confirm the PoAh data to add blocks to the chain. Following accepting a valid block, the user gets the hash 
value from the previous block to save into the current block and computes a hash value to connect to the next 
block.

Execution time
Compared to standard PoW , PoAh offers a key advantage of reduced execution time without compromising on 
security. PoW , which takes about 10 min to validate a single block, is simply not practical for IoT use. In response 
to this challenge, PoAh employs cryptographic authentication for block validation, a process that is rapid and 
significantly reduces execution time. This makes PoAh a highly suitable option for IIoT networks with limited 
resources. The execution time is the total time needed to complete one transaction request authentication, which 
is defined as follows:
 ∂T txr = Tch − Ti
Here Tchrepresents the specific node timestamp which is added to the blockchain network. Ti is the initial 
timestamp of node transactions request. The proposed authentication consensus mechanism provides better 
execution time, which is suitable for IoT applications.
Security
Integrating PoAh as a consensus algorithm into blockchain-based IoT frameworks ensures an IoT framework’s 
sustained security, providing real-time security and accurate data authentication. The security needed for 
cryptocurrency is different from that required for IoT systems. PoAh, apart from the reverse hash calculation 
needed for block validation, integrates with the current PoW cryptography paradigm. This integration ensures

Our experiments showed that the blockchain-assisted edge computing architecture significantly reduced 
latency and improved service time compared to conventional IIoT systems. The inclusion of edge nodes, which 
localized data processing using blockchain, was the main reason for the decreased latency. The blockchain layer, 
with its trust mechanism, ensured data integrity and security for transactions between IoT devices and edge 
nodes. Importantly, the system successfully repelled simulated security risks, including replay and man-in-
the-middle attacks, demonstrating the robustness of the system. The proposed system performs well with a 
moderate number of IoT devices; however, performance decreased when the blockchain network’s participating 
edge nodes grew above 100. This bottleneck is due to the increased challenge of reaching a consensus with more 
nodes.
Conclusion
Industrial IoT modernizes innovative sectors by integrating cutting-edge technologies. One such technology 
that has drawn significant interest from academia and industry is blockchain. An intelligent industry may benefit 
from the advanced characteristics that blockchain technology brings, such as higher efficiency, protection, 
consistency, trust, and decentralization. In this study, we provide a blockchain-based framework for intelligent 
edge computing. A safe, lightweight, decentralized private blockchain-based IIoT network that can perform 
several crucial tasks, including trusted machine management, data storage, and user and device registration, 
is made possible by the PoAh-based blockchain system. Specifically, we present an edge-level implementation 
of authentication that lowers the computational burden and improves the industry platform’s security. Many 
performance characteristics are considered while evaluating the suggested architecture’s efficiency. The 
experimental findings demonstrated that the proposed design outperformed other cutting-edge approaches. 
Ultimately, we used the suggested design to convert a conventional fruit processing facility to realize the 
enormous potential of blockchain technology for an intelligent industry sector.
